name: Case Study
description: A real-world case worked through: the facts, the context, what went wrong, the options, a judgement to debate, and the principle it teaches. For law, commerce, management and medicine.
audience: Law judgments, business cases, patient cases, ethics scenarios.

signals.why: case teaching is common in this subject

slides.guidance: Title naming the case in {topic}, with a subtitle saying what principle it teaches.
What students will be able to analyse or judge after working through {topic}.
The one fact of the case that makes it worth studying. Only facts in the source or well established.
The background students need: who was involved, what the situation was. Three or four points.
What led to the problem in {topic}, and what followed from it.
The courses of action available, compared on their consequences.
One or two questions asking students what they would decide, and why.
The principle this case teaches, and how it applies to other cases.
